Key.English:
Sets the cells of uniforms, vests,
backpacks, crates and vehicles, as
class:size pairs separated by commas.

A number is that many cells, laid out
like the container's own pockets or
pouches. WxH is one compartment W cells
wide and H high - join several with +.

Example:
V_PlateCarrier1_rgr:20,
B_AssaultPack_rgr:30,
B_Carryall_cbr:6x4+2x3+2x3

Use the uniform's or vest's own class.
A class counts for every class based on
it, unless that one is listed itself.

Wins over the rules text, config and
the load per cell. A number goes up to
320 cells, compartments up to 8 wide
and 40 high, 24 of them and 320 cells
in all. The rules text does the same:
class=B_Carryall_Base+ > grid=6x4+2x3

A mission can give one crate, vehicle
or unit's uniform, vest or backpack
container its own grid, which wins
over all of this: the object variable
einv_grid, e.g. "6x4+2x3".

Entries that cannot be read are left
out and named in the RPT.
Log backpack drops to the RPT

Writes every step of taking a worn
backpack off onto the ground to the
RPT, each line starting "einv drop:":
the request, the take-off, the pile it
goes onto, the backpack added there,
its contents filled in and anything
settled afterwards.

For tests only - leave it off.

How far from a player piles on the
ground and crates show in the loot
column on their own, in metres - and
how far away anything can still be
changed while the inventory is open.

Only what the player sees from where
they stand counts: nothing through
walls or from another floor.

Vehicles and bodies show when they
are opened, as before.
